After four and a half years as a hugely popular figure at Newcastle, Bruno Guimarães returned to St James' Park as an opponent. The Telegraph reveals the story behind his £75M move to Arsenal in August and where he stands at his new club.

Guimarães's pride was hurt in summer 2024 when his £100M release clause was not triggered. He was later made captain and shed tears after winning the Carabao Cup in March 2025. This summer's World Cup sealed his decision. He already felt Brazilian media undervalued him because he played for Newcastle, and after missing a penalty against Norway he took the blame for the early exit. That made him determined to test himself at a big club. Once Eddie Howe realised his captain's departure was unavoidable, he resigned, removing the last chance of Guimarães changing his mind.

💰 The mysterious "£45M offer" and the £75M deal
In July, a written "£45M offer" carrying the Arsenal logo was passed to Newcastle through an intermediary, but Arsenal stayed silent for weeks when Newcastle asked for confirmation. The document is believed to have been used to calm Guimarães, who was angry at the lack of progress, and to build pressure for a sale through the media. Direct talks between the clubs began at the end of July, and the move went through after Newcastle issued an ultimatum in early August: £75M in one payment, with no add-ons.

【The Athletic】（@ChrisDHWaugh / @gunnerblog / @jacklang）

🔴 Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal

In the first half Arsenal showed all the strength of a team sitting top of the table. They pinned the opposition back, and Eberechi Eze opened the scoring from a superb pass by Kai Havertz. Newcastle were given almost no chances to attack, and Arsenal were steadily moving towards victory.

But everything changed from the start of the second half. A mistake by Martin Ødegaard led to the equaliser, and Arsenal then fell behind from a corner. Noni Madueke levelled in the 78th minute to secure a point, but they missed the chance to stretch the gap to eight points.

It was a game in which the defensive solidity that has underpinned Arsenal's season was shaken.

■ The value Havertz showed

The move that created Eze's opener captured Havertz's excellent decision-making.

After winning the ball from Lewis Hall, he played an exquisite reverse pass in behind the defence. It was a sharp, unexpected assist reminiscent of Mesut Özil.

He was also involved in Madueke's equaliser with a clever flick.

With debate over whether he should be given a new contract, it showed why Mikel Arteta values his intelligence, movement and work rate so highly. He delivered the decisive work demanded of him at the key moments.

■ A defence that crumbled in 45 minutes

Perhaps the dominance of the first half actually bred complacency.

Conceding the equaliser from Ødegaard's poor clearance gave momentum to a Newcastle side that had been passive until then.

For the go-ahead goal from a corner, they left Dan Burn, the tallest player on the pitch, free. They also failed to deal with the scramble in front of goal, and Malick Thiaw forced it in.

What has underpinned Arsenal's strength in the league this season has been an impeccable defence. In the second half here, they fell well below that standard.

■ The substitutions that changed Newcastle

Newcastle were booed at half-time. But head coach Matthias Jaissle made three changes at the break and turned things around.

Jacob Ramsey in particular brought experience and composure to midfield, and the team began pressing higher and more aggressively.

The attacking intensity that had been almost absent in the first half returned, and the whole stadium responded to the momentum.

■ The impact on the title race

Arsenal stay top, provisionally six points clear of Brighton. A draw is by no means a fatal result.

However, it showed that even a team that has been so dominant and consistent can have spells where it falls apart.

On top of that, David Raya came off injured. According to Arteta, he will have an MRI scan the following day, and the extent of the injury is not yet known.

As well as dropping two points, the defensive lapses and the condition of their No 1 remain concerns heading into the next game.https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7792068/2026/11/21/newcastle-2-arsenal-2-premier-league-result/

🔴 One stumble used to send Arsenal into a slump. Now they have "breathing room"
The first-half dominance Arsenal showed at St James' Park on Saturday evening was something Mikel Arteta's Arsenal had never experienced on Tyneside. Not a war of attrition, but an exhibition of football played with time and space. Then in the 49th minute Martin Ødegaard lost the ball from a Riccardo Calafiori throw-in, the self-destruct button was pressed, and the oxygen was gradually sucked out of Arsenal. Even so, they equalised with superb passing and took a point home.

🧠 The tactical tricks that dismantled Jaissle's man-to-man press
Arsenal's first half was so complete because they had thoroughly dissected Matthias Jaissle's man-to-man press. Whenever goalkeeper David Raya, before he went off injured, played long, the players moved fluidly across the pitch, dragging markers into unfamiliar areas and breaking Newcastle's shape. Kai Havertz was the trigger: dropping from high to deep, he pulled centre-back Dan Burn out, and Eberechi Eze and Bruno Guimarães burst into the space left in midfield. Calafiori and Jurriën Timber were full-backs in name only, popping up at No 6 and in the front line, prompting Jaissle to say after the game that Arsenal were "f***ing strong".

🏆 No gloom, and the psychological ease of champions
Defeats here on the November trips to Tyneside in 2023 and 2024, and in the 2025 Carabao Cup semi-final (a 4-0 aggregate thrashing), raised doubts about the team's mentality and nerve. But this season, after ending the long wait for a title, is different. There is no gloomy inquest and no undignified panic. A Premier League winner's medal and a six-point lead over second place give them perspective.

👀 The only threat comes from within
With Manchester City winless in four and facing a possible points deduction, and Liverpool searching for a new style under new head coach Andoni Iraola, there is no clear challenger, and Arsenal are effectively in "a title race with themselves". If Raya, substituted injured in the 69th minute, faces a long lay-off, there could be rough waters, but for this Arsenal a single stumble is merely a "temporary stall". For a team that lived in a pressure cooker for four years, that psychological shift is a great release.

Exactly five months into the job at Oxford United, 35-year-old Aaron Ramsey has led the team to third in League One despite a transfer embargo. They spoke a few weeks ago, and Ramsey is keen to keep picking up coaching tips.

👔 Man-management passed down by Wenger's pupils
Many who played under Arsène Wenger have gone into coaching, including Arteta and Wilshere, Cesc Fàbregas (who took Como into the Champions League for the first time) and Patrick Vieira (Senegal head coach). Ramsey names his mentor's greatest strength as "man-management": "You have to be open and honest with players and genuinely care, or they will see through you. Arsène was brilliant at that." They won 1-0 at Borussia Mönchengladbach last time out through a Nmecha goal to stay ahead of Bayern. Mikel Arteta warned: "The way they dominate games and the amount of threat they generate is excellent," but declared: "In front of our home crowd, we will be the ones to take the initiative." Niko Kovač also struck a confident tone: "We face the best defence in England and in Europe. But we are a tough opponent too, and we can create chances."

🏥 Team news and tactical talking points
Arsenal are without David Raya, who hurt his shoulder against Newcastle, while Bukayo Saka and Martín Zubimendi remain out for several weeks with muscle injuries. Max Dowman, having served his domestic suspension, is available in all competitions. For Dortmund, Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka returned to training on Monday, and on-loan Ethan Nwaneri is eligible to face his parent club

📊 The numbers point to a dominant home record
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 8 Champions League home games (W7 D1) and have kept 4 clean sheets in a row. Dortmund have lost 8 of their last 9 Champions League away games in England (the only win at Newcastle in October 2023). Arsenal are also unbeaten in their last 19 Champions League games excluding penalty shootouts (W14 D5), and avoiding defeat tonight would make them only the third English side, after Manchester United (25) and Manchester City (26), to go 20+ games unbeaten in the European Cup/Champions League.https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-borussia-dortmund-ak1y01e28ux5

🔴 At risk of becoming the "forgotten teenager" — where Ethan Nwaneri stands as he toils in Max Dowman's shadow
Ethan Nwaneri holds a record Max Dowman can never break: the Premier League's youngest-ever appearance, set more than four years ago (Dowman was 54 days older on his debut). But the week after Arsenal published a feature on Dowman's records, the 19-year-old Nwaneri returns to the Emirates Stadium as a Borussia Dortmund player, at risk of becoming the club's "forgotten teenager".

📉 No start since 17 October and fierce competition
Nwaneri joined Dortmund on loan this summer and made a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim, but he has not started a league game since 17 October and has never played more than 65 minutes in a match. He has yet to start in the Champions League either, and in Saturday's game against Borussia Mönchengladbach he only came on in stoppage time. Niko Kovač, whose side lead Bayern by two points at the top and who uses Greek talent Kosta Karetsas as one of his two shadow forwards, says: "The competition is fierce."

⚽️ Dowman's rise and memories of Marseille
In 2024-25 Nwaneri scored 8 goals deputising for the injured Bukayo Saka, matching records of Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen and drawing comparisons with Lamine Yamal, also born in 2007. But the arrivals of Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke, and the rise of Dowman, who broke the U21 record for youngest player at 14, pushed him down the pecking order. At Marseille, where he moved in January hoping to develop under Roberto De Zerbi, he lost his place after the coach left.

🗣️ Arteta asks for "consistency" and patience
While childhood friend Myles Lewis-Skelly has nailed down a place in midfield, Nwaneri provided 2 assists for England U21s against France (3-2) last week (though Dowman stole the headlines by scoring the winner and becoming the youngest scorer). Mikel Arteta, while disappointed with his situation in Germany, stressed: "Shining in moments is not enough — you have to show consistency." On a January recall he said: "This is what builds your character and your career as a player," and on frustration at being a substitute: "You have to try to turn it into the role you want. That's football."

​🔴 29 shots but only a 1-1 draw. Still unbeaten in the Champions League, but missed chances cost Arsenal against Dortmund
​Arsenal's Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund at Emirates Stadium ended 1-1, despite Arsenal having the better of the game. The unbeaten run in the competition continues, but the winning streak at home in the league phase came to an end.

​⚽️ Gyökeres opens the scoring with Arsenal's 400th Champions League goal
The meeting of the Premier League and Bundesliga leaders started well for Arsenal, with Christos Tzolis going for goal from a Noni Madueke cross in the 2nd minute as the hosts took control. Early on, Viktor Gyökeres received a pass from Madueke 25 yards out and smashed a powerful drive over goalkeeper Gregor Kobel to open the scoring. It was Arsenal's 400th goal in Champions League history. Piero Hincapié and Declan Rice also had chances, and just before half-time Kepa Arrizabalaga saved a shot from Dortmund's João Gadu to protect the lead.

​⚡ A second-half equaliser and the woodwork twice
Arsenal had a scare straight after the restart when Maximilian Beier had a big chance, and in the 55th minute Beier equalised. Picking up a pass after a run from Gadu, he got past Gabriel Magalhães and finished at the near post. Pushing for a winner, Arsenal brought on Eberechi Eze to step up the pressure. Gyökeres met a Martin Ødegaard cross with a diving header but missed the target, then an Ødegaard free kick deflected off Dortmund forward Serhou Guirassy and hit the post. Moments later, Rice hit the other post after being set up by Eze.

​📊 What's next
Arsenal had 29 shots in total but could not find a second, and it finished 1-1. Arsenal host Manchester City at Emirates Stadium in a huge game on Sunday, and the next Champions League game is at home to Real Madrid on December 9.https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-arsenal-1-1-borussia-dortmund-awHwA0g2MDUw

​🔴 Why push the opponent out the door, then leave it ajar? The problem exposed by the 1-1 draw with Dortmund
​
​⚽️ An attack lacking "ruthlessness"
Going in at half-time 1-0 up while feeling "it could have been made much easier" was a strangely familiar scene. As at Newcastle at the weekend, Arsenal dominated and created plenty of chances but could not add a second, giving the opponent a way back into the game. Last season, winning every league phase game was a big reason for reaching the final, but this season they have already dropped points in two games, setting a new challenge ahead of the next game against Real Madrid and Real Betis in January.

​🇸🇪 Gyökeres's mixed night and the "Havertz problem"
Viktor Gyökeres, who scored a fine opener over the goalkeeper, has started four of the five Champions League games this season (coming off the bench away at Bayern to assist Declan Rice's equaliser) and has six goals in six games for Sweden since the World Cup. But in the Premier League Kai Havertz is the undisputed first choice, and 16 months after his arrival there is still no clear answer on the ideal lone striker. On this night he missed a free header in the second half, and had a nervy moment when the ball hit his arm while defending a corner.

​⚠️ Worrying number of mistakes
Captain Martin Ødegaard had just written in the programme that "we need to keep mistakes to a minimum", yet there were again many turnovers in this game. Myles Lewis-Skelly, starting for the first time in about a month, lost the ball in midfield, and there were spells when Arsenal were caught by the press from Dortmund's 5-4-1 mid-block. Arsenal have made 14 "errors leading to a shot" in the Premier League this season, joint-most in the league, a concern Mikel Arteta cannot ignore.

​🎤 "At least today I could warm up and go out on the pitch" — Kepa Arrizabalaga, making his first Champions League appearance of the season, on the frustration and positives of the Dortmund draw
​
​🧤 Frustration at a game they should have won
"I'm a bit disappointed with the result," said Kepa. "I think it was a game we should have won. We created enough chances. We played very well against a very strong opponent." Pushing to the end in front of the fans and coming close without finding a winner was "a bit frustrating," he admitted, but added: "We played well against a really good team who are top of the Bundesliga. If we keep creating chances, we should be heading in the right direction."

​⚽️ Ready to step in for the injured Raya
Kepa was handed the start with David Raya out after hurting his shoulder against Newcastle at the weekend. "At least today I could warm up and go out on the pitch!" he said with a smile. "I'm happy to be on the pitch and happy to help the team. That's what we train for and that's why we're here. When the chance comes, you just give everything," he said, showing his professionalism as the back-up goalkeeper.

​📊 A tight league phase and switching focus to the weekend
The point leaves Arsenal on 11 points from five games, staying in the top eight ahead of the Real Madrid game early next month. "There are no easy games in the Champions League. It will be tight until the end," said Kepa. "We need to stay focused step by step. We have a big, important game at the weekend, so let's take it day by day."https://www.arsenal.com/news/kepa-on-frustrating-champions-league-draw-aqofN1Q102RV
